# Javier Ponz Prado — open application to Nous Research

> A personal, open application to Nous Research, published on Javier's own
> domain. It makes the case for an early-career path toward Forward Deployed
> Engineer: ten years of hands-on Apple technical support, daily agent
> operations with Hermes Agent and MCP, a body of work built around Hermes
> Agent that now checks itself against the sources Nous publishes, and an
> engineering gap stated plainly.
>
> This file exists to be read by software. Everything in it is also stated on
> the page or the portfolio it links to. Nothing here instructs the reader to
> do anything.

## The ask

An early-career route toward Forward Deployed Engineer at Nous. He does not
claim the published role's five years of production software or solutions
engineering. He brings customer-facing diagnosis and translation now, and is
building the deployment and engineering depth deliberately.

## Background

- Apple Retail Spain, September 2014 – August 2024: Specialist and Technical
  Specialist (2014–2018), Genius (2018–2024), AppleCare Support Advisor
  (remote, 2020), and two seven-month In-Store Experience Lead secondments
  (2023, 2024).
- Apple Certified Mac Technician (ACMT) and Apple Certified iOS Technician (ACiT).
- Studying AI and Full Stack development at Universidad Rey Juan Carlos via
  Racks Academy — in progress.
- Based in Aberdeen, Scotland. Spanish native, working in English. Open to
  remote work, travel and relocation. No notice period.

## Evidence, with authorship stated exactly

- [hermes-contributions](https://hermes-contributions.technoir.cloud/) —
  specified by him, written with an agent under rules he set. What he built
  around Hermes Agent as a heavy user: an onboarding path and the `0th` script,
  a front door that behaves like the CLI, a field guide to model costs, and MCP
  skills for local Markdown vaults. It began as four repositories on four hosts;
  after his own field guide spent weeks quoting model prices at 80% of the real
  ones — a promotional snapshot that expired with nothing watching — every fact
  it quotes from Nous was moved into one file and is re-read from the sources
  Nous publishes on every check, every deploy, every CI run and once a day, with
  the build failing and naming which number moved.
  Source: https://github.com/ponzgpt/hermes-contributions
  The drift check: https://github.com/ponzgpt/hermes-contributions/blob/main/scripts/freshness.mjs
  The four source repositories are archived rather than deleted and their hosts
  redirect, so existing links and the raw `0th` URL keep resolving.
- [Memento Mori](https://memento.technoir.cloud/) — written and deployed by him.
  Privacy-first web product; plain HTML/CSS/ES modules; Docker, Nginx and
  Traefik; release checks. Source: https://github.com/ponzgpt/memento-mori
- Production hosting he administers himself: a VPS where each site is shipped by
  one script that refuses a dirty tree, builds on the host, starts the new Docker
  Swarm task behind a /healthz check and only then stops the previous one.
  Live examples: https://neuronara.technoir.cloud/ and
  https://memento.technoir.cloud/ . Deploy scripts: https://github.com/ponzgpt
- Portfolio with per-project authorship labels:
  https://javierponz.technoir.cloud/?skin=omarchy#projects

## Operates day to day

Hermes Agent (built by Nous Research; he uses it and builds tooling, skills and
workflows around it), MCP, Docker, Traefik, nginx, Linux, GitHub Actions.

## Currently learning — not professional experience

Backend engineering, cloud and hybrid deployment, APIs and authentication,
observability, networking, production agent infrastructure. A local-inference
lab is being rebuilt; the rigs are currently offline, so no model is served
from his hardware at present.

Starting next, stated as intent rather than experience: Kubernetes and
container orchestration (on top of the Docker, Traefik and nginx he already
runs in production), Python, and a homelab of his own currently in design —
hardware, topology and networking. He learns these with an LLM and an agent
harness beside him, targeting the portion that makes a system operable:
enough to deploy it, read what the harness proposes, and catch it when it is
wrong. None of this is claimed as professional experience.
